# tfcensus report inventory

inventory counts the managed resource instances in an index written by tfcensus inventory
--save-index, per unit and TF type, with the instances another state also manages. It is
what the inventory tool of tfcensus mcp returns.

## Usage

```sh
tfcensus report inventory [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--account` | AWS account ID | string |  |  | [`accounts.include`](/reference/config#accounts-include) |  |
| `--index` | state index from tfcensus inventory --save-index | string |  |  |  |  |
| `--region` | AWS region | string |  | 34 values; shell completion lists them | [`regions`](/reference/config#regions) |  |
| `--type` | TF resource type glob, such as aws\_iam\_\* | string |  |  |  |  |
| `--unit` | unit path glob, \* matches / too | string |  |  |  |  |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command.

## Output formats

`--format` accepts `tty`, `plain`, `json`. Without it, the format is `tty` when stdout is a terminal and `plain` otherwise. Formats are described on the [global flags](/cli/global-flags) page.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
tfcensus report inventory --index index.json.zst --account 111111111111 --type 'aws_iam_*'
```
